result:
Two branches being merged share no common ancestor commit → git assumes they're different projects and refuses (default since 2.9).

Usual cause: repo created on GitHub with README/license, plus separate `git init` locally, then `git pull`. Other causes: remote points at wrong repo (check `git remote -v`), shallow clone (`git fetch --unshallow`), or history rewritten upstream.

If both sides are meant to be one project, allow it once:

```
git pull origin main --allow-unrelated-histories
```

Resolve any conflicts (typically README/.gitignore), commit, push. Flag only needed this one time; afterwards histories are joined.

If remote holds only an auto-generated README you don't care about, `git push --force origin main` also fixes it, but that permanently overwrites the remote's commits, so only do it if nothing there is worth keeping and nobody else has cloned it.

Separately: chisle plugin has a `[CHISLE]` statusline badge that isn't configured. Want me to set it up?
